title: Kahana vs Vimeo: The Club Layer for Video
excerpt: Vimeo is long-form video hosting, reach, and subscriptions. Kahana is the club layer and discovery signal for learning from video.
defaultImageQuery: Vimeo The club layer and discovery signal for learning from video.
seoTitle: Kahana vs Vimeo | The Club Layer for Video
metaDescription: Vimeo is long-form video hosting, reach, and subscriptions. Kahana is the club layer and discovery signal for learning from video.

columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: ≈300M users globally (2023); self-serve paying subscribers ~1.5M+ by 2020 and ≈1.28M in Q3 2024, plus ~3,800 enterprise clients.
Revenue USD 433M in 2022; ≈USD 417M over 12 months to Sep 2023; Q3 2024 revenue USD 104.5M.
No ads on site or embeds; monetizes via subscriptions/services. Creators can sell videos (since 2013) or subscriptions (since 2015) with ~10% platform cut.
≈4.1% online video platform market share as of Feb 2024, far behind YouTube and Netflix.

strengths.title: Ad-free, professional hosting
strengths.detail: High-quality ad-free hosting for businesses, filmmakers, and creatives needing polished embeds and branded experiences.

strengths.title: SaaS features for business video
strengths.detail: Livestreaming, analytics, player customization, password-protected videos, and marketing integrations.

strengths.title: Monetization options for creators
strengths.detail: Sell individual videos or subscriptions with a relatively small (~10%) platform cut.

strengths.title: Better fit for B2B and brand sites than YouTube
strengths.detail: Ad-free embeds, customization, and no algorithmic related-video distraction, strong for brand sites and course platforms.

weaknesses.title: Much smaller audience than YouTube
weaknesses.detail: ~300M users and hundreds of millions in revenue vs YouTube’s billions of users and tens of billions in revenue.

weaknesses.title: Paid-subscriber growth challenges
weaknesses.detail: Self-serve paying subscribers declined slightly (1.5M → 1.28M); revenue per user has fluctuated.

weaknesses.title: Less discovery and social engagement
weaknesses.detail: Primarily hosting, not social discovery, weaker for organic audience growth vs YouTube or TikTok.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Vimeo is long-form video hosting, reach, and subscriptions. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Vimeo is an ad-free video hosting, sharing, and services platform that operates as SaaS for creators and businesses, offering high-definition video delivery, streaming tools, and monetization options.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Vimeo side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Vimeo you can use Long-form video and Memberships as first-class product jobs. You need distribution, search, ads, or a native player at platform scale.

Using Kahana with Vimeo

You can use both. Vimeo keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep hosting and distribution on Vimeo. Put the lectures or series that deserve a shelf into Kahana hubs, ideally via embed, then discuss them in a Club. Reach stays on Vimeo; Kahana is where the work is findable after the tab is closed, and where you can grow an audience around it.
